name: Niseko United
locality: Kutchan and Niseko towns: Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village and Annupuri
operator: Four separately operated resorts sold on the joint Niseko United All Mountain Pass (Grand Hirafu is run as 'Niseko Tokyu Grand Hirafu')

source.note: Piste reference data — confirm at source. Approximate Grand Hirafu base / Hirafu village position; Hanazono, Niseko Village and Annupuri have their own bases

Search summary: base 240 m, summit 1,308 m (Mt. Niseko Annupuri). Vertical derived as the difference. Reference, confirm: the highest lifts stop below the peak (about 1,200 m); the summit is reached on foot through backcountry gates

source.note: Search summary of third-party listings (OnTheSnow / skiresort.info): 73 runs (34% novice, 37% intermediate, 29% advanced), about 42 km of marked runs, 30 lifts (6 gondolas, 24 chairlifts) across the four resorts. Attribution between listings approximate; the same summary gave about 2,191 acres (not stored — acres are for North American resorts)

Piste reference data — confirm at source. Only features Piste is confident about are set; everything else is unknown (null), not 'not offered'. Night skiing is offered (notably at Grand Hirafu); ski-in lodging exists in Hirafu and at Niseko Village. Hours and extent not on file

character: Four linked resorts on the flanks of Mt. Niseko Annupuri in western Hokkaido — Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village and Annupuri — sold on one All Mountain Pass. The area is known for frequent, light powder snow and gate-controlled backcountry access, and Hirafu village is the main international base.
learning: About a third of the runs are rated novice (search summary). Reference, confirm: each of the four resorts has ski schools and lower-mountain beginner slopes.

announcedOpening.text: All four Niseko United resorts scheduled to open 28 Nov 2026 (snow permitting); closing dates vary by resort, the latest 5 May 2027.

source.note: Search summary of a third-party article (japanskiexperience.com); also listed in batch 2026-27 opening-date summaries. Confirm on niseko.ne.jp

announcedClosing.text: Latest scheduled closing among the four resorts; the others close earlier (per-resort dates not captured).

source.note: Search summary of a third-party article

season.typicalText: Late November or early December to early May, varying by resort
season.notes: 2025-26: all four resorts were scheduled to open on 29 Nov 2025, but the opening was postponed for lack of snow; by 5 Dec 2025 all had opened with limited terrain (search summaries citing rhythmjapan.com and Niseko news). The 2026-27 opening is a plan and depends on snow cover.

prices.note: Peak-season price, 24 Dec 2026 – 28 Feb 2027. Ages 4–12 ¥8,100; ages 13–15 and seniors 65+ ¥11,500. Value- and regular-season prices were not captured.

transfers.name: Airport buses and shared shuttles from New Chitose
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: seasonal ski buses and shared shuttles run from New Chitose Airport to Hirafu and the other Niseko bases (roughly 2.5–3 h). Operators, fares and schedules are not on file.

transfers.name: JR trains to Kutchan or Niseko station
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: JR from New Chitose Airport via Sapporo and Otaru to Kutchan (for Hirafu) or Niseko station, then local bus or taxi; changes needed.

transfers.name: Inter-resort shuttle buses
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: winter buses link Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village and Annupuri.
